summary: The repaired five-question batch works, but normal generation excludes all sole-witness 3×3 triangular matrices, including the canonical example. Sampled mathematics, native grading, delivery and rendering passed. Package unchanged.

source_analysis.skill: Describe a square numeric matrix by inspecting zeros relative to the main diagonal and choosing the most specific supplied class.
reasoning_steps: Locate the main diagonal; inspect all strictly upper and strictly lower entries.
Zeros below imply upper triangular; zeros above imply lower triangular. Both imply diagonal; use the best description rather than any true superclass.
For a strict triangular result, exhibit a nonzero on the permitted side to exclude diagonal and the opposite orientation.
invariants: Square matrix, direct classification, no operations or transformed matrices.
Definitions inspect zeros on an entire side, not a predetermined witness cell.
Best description resolves nesting: nonidentity diagonal precedes triangular.
Keep the five-label radio bank and short explanatory method.
permitted_variations: Upper versus lower orientation, matrix letter, signs and magnitudes, diagonal entries including zero, placement and number of nonzeros on permitted side, 2x2 versus 3x3 within easy workload.
Moderate: diagonal values can vary while excluding identity unless explicitly supported as a conservative prerequisite-based extension.
Witness a21/a12 is incidental: any strictly lower/upper coordinate may carry the sole nonzero.
Bank order is incidental and may vary independently of correctness.

findings.description: level_guard and catalog require at least ceil(n(n−1)/4) nonzero off-diagonal entries. For 3×3 this rejects every strict triangular matrix with one witness, including canonical A=[[-2,0,0],[6,-1,0],[0,0,0]]. Such matrices still require inspecting the same zero region; the claimed scan-workload reason does not justify excluding the canonical pattern. This is a generator-domain defect, not incorrect sampled answers or a demonstrated stored-instance defect.
